subject: art-design
title: Cubism & Surrealism
welcome_lead: Picasso's fractured shapes and Dali's dream worlds.
meta_desc: KS3 art movements: Cubism and Surrealism explained.
final_note: 20th-century art broke the rules of what a picture should show.

concepts.def: Style breaking subjects into geometric shapes.
Style showing dreams and the unconscious.

walkthroughs.body_html: Cubism was started by Picasso and Braque around 1907. They smashed objects into geometric shapes and showed multiple viewpoints at the same time — a face from front and side at once.
Surrealism came in the 1920s. Artists like Salvador Dali and Magritte painted dream-like images: melting clocks, floating apples, impossible scenes — exploring the unconscious mind.
Cubism broke up the look of real objects; Surrealism kept objects realistic but put them in impossible situations. Both rejected ordinary appearance.

mcqs.q: What did Renaissance artists rediscover that medieval art lacked?
options: Linear perspective and naturalistic representation of the human body.
The unconscious mind, dreams, and Freudian psychology.

mcqs.q: What can line in a composition imply, even without representing an object?
options: Only the outline of an object.
Movement, direction, emotion, and visual rhythm.
